title: Bookkeeping & reconciliations
summary: I can help you get your records up to date, match them to the bank and work through anything that does not look right.
outputs: Updated sales and purchase ledgers with supporting-document references
Bank, credit-card and control-account reconciliation schedules
A query log for missing records, unmatched entries and proposed corrections
scope: We’ll agree which business and period to cover, the software to use and how much work the records need. Any proposed corrections and open questions will go to your practice’s reviewer.
need: The business and period you need help with, plus the software you use.
Bank and card statements, bookkeeping exports and relevant invoices, shared through an agreed secure route after we agree the work.
A short note about any backlog, missing records or balances you are worried about.
steps: First, we agree what needs doing
We talk through the period, number of accounts and condition of the records. I confirm what I will work on, what you will receive and who will review any changes.
I check the starting point
I compare the opening balances with the previous records and check that the statements and bookkeeping exports cover the same dates. If something is missing, I ask for it before going further.
I work through the transactions
I match receipts and payments to the ledger and supporting records. I look into duplicates, missing entries and items posted to the wrong place. I keep a note of anything I need you to explain.
I explain the differences
I separate genuine timing differences from errors. Any proposed correction has a reason and a source reference. I do not add an unexplained adjustment just to make the totals agree.
I hand over the reconciliation
You receive the reconciliation, the proposed corrections and a short list of open questions. Items needing approval go to your reviewer, and anything still awaiting evidence stays clearly marked.
pricing: The quote depends on how many bank or card accounts are involved, transaction volume, the number of months and how much investigation is needed. A tidy month of records and a historic backlog will need different amounts of work.

title: Accounts preparation & working papers
summary: I can organise the schedules and supporting records your reviewer needs for month-end or year-end accounts.
outputs: Accrual and prepayment schedules with a stated basis
Selected balance-sheet reconciliations and proposed journals
Close checklist, supporting references and unresolved reviewer queries
scope: We’ll agree the reporting period, the records available and the schedules you need. I’ll prepare the draft work for your practice to review and approve.
need: The reporting period, deadline and the schedules your practice needs.
The trial balance, previous working papers and relevant supporting records, shared securely once scope is agreed.
Details of any missing invoices, uncertain balances or adjustments already under discussion.
steps: We agree the pack you need
I ask which balances and schedules you want covered, who will review the file and when it is needed. This keeps a selected working-paper pack separate from a complete accounts engagement.
I check the records fit together
I compare the trial balance with the ledgers and supporting schedules. I note missing records, unusual balances and questions that could hold up the close.
I prepare the schedules
I work through the agreed balances, including relevant accruals, prepayments and reconciliations. I show the calculation, the period it relates to and the record it came from.
I document proposed changes
I set out proposed journals and explain why they are needed. Estimates and assumptions are labelled, so your reviewer can see where confirmation is still required.
I prepare the handover
I send the agreed schedules, references, close checklist and open queries. The reviewer can see what has been checked and what still needs a decision before sign-off.
pricing: The quote depends on the number of schedules, the condition of the trial balance, the amount of missing information and the deadline. We agree whether you need selected schedules or a wider preparation pack.

title: VAT & CIS preparation support
summary: I can help your practice prepare VAT and CIS records, check the supporting balances and flag questions for review.
outputs: Organised records supporting VAT and CIS preparation
Balance reconciliations and checks on deductions and supporting records
A list of missing information and items requiring reviewer confirmation
scope: We’ll agree the period, software, records and review process first. My work here is preparation support; we’ll confirm who is authorised to approve and submit it.
need: The period, software and preparation work your practice needs help with.
Relevant bookkeeping records, invoices and subcontractor payment records through an agreed secure route.
Your practice’s instructions, reviewer details and confirmation of who is responsible for submission.
steps: We agree the preparation and review roles
Before I start, we confirm the period, records to use, checks required and who will review and submit the work. The scope is preparation support within your practice’s processes.
I check that the records are there
I check the dates and look for missing invoices, payment details or other gaps. I list questions early so there is time to resolve them.
I prepare the supporting checks
I reconcile the relevant balances and check the supporting entries and deductions against your practice’s instructions. I flag anything unusual instead of guessing at its treatment.
I separate questions from completed work
I record missing evidence, uncertain entries and items that need a reviewer’s decision. Your practice can see which checks are complete and what is still open.
I hand the preparation to your reviewer
I provide the supporting records and query list for review. Corrections and approval follow your practice’s process; submission responsibility remains with the agreed authorised person.
pricing: The quote depends on whether the work covers VAT, CIS or both, the period, record volume, missing information and the checks your practice requires. I explain the preparation scope before you agree to a fee.

title: Management reporting & construction costs
summary: I can help you see where project costs have moved, what that means for the margin and which questions need attention.
outputs: Project cost schedules and budget-versus-actual comparisons
Profitability reports with stated assumptions and variance commentary
Management questions, including a clear distinction between profit and cash
scope: We’ll agree the projects, reporting dates and costs to include. I’ll explain the assumptions and flag incomplete records so management can review the report properly.
need: The project or reporting period you want to review and the questions you need answered.
The budget, actual costs, project income and relevant supporting records, shared securely after scope is agreed.
Your cost categories and any known late invoices, outstanding income or costs that have not yet been allocated.
steps: We decide what the report needs to answer
We agree the project, reporting dates and cost categories. I ask whether you need a completed-project report, a budget comparison or a regular management update.
I organise the project records
I bring together the budget, actual costs and project income. I check that the records cover the same period and flag costs or income that may be missing or assigned to the wrong project.
I compare budget with actual costs
I work through materials, labour, subcontractors, plant hire and maintenance where relevant. I show each difference and look for a supporting explanation.
I explain the margin and the cash position
I show how the project result is calculated and state what is included. If cash information is in scope, I separate amounts earned or incurred from money received or paid.
I turn the findings into useful questions
You receive the report, plain-language commentary and a short list of points for management. Assumptions, incomplete records and questions about late costs are visible.
pricing: The quote depends on the number of projects, reporting periods, cost categories and how much work is needed to organise the inputs. We also agree whether this is a one-off report or recurring support.
